Facial expressions must fit the scene: joy may be open, grief stays tender, hardship shows focused care, and stillness feels calm rather than performed.
No asset enters page code until it has passed a direct visual comparison with the identity reference.

birth-of-christ.html.tone: Amid fear for Jerusalem, Isaiah brings a word from the Lord. Read the encounter and the promise of Immanuel in its setting.
The quiet hills invite us to consider Micah’s promise about Bethlehem and the ruler who would come from it.
Nephi sees a mother with the Son of God in her arms. Through this vision, he comes to understand the love of God.
The angel brings good tidings of the Lord’s coming among His people. Benjamin will share this witness of the Savior’s birth and saving mission.
Alma teaches that the Son will be born of Mary and take upon Himself the pains and infirmities of His people. His coming brings help for the whole human journey.
Samuel announces the signs that will accompany the Savior’s birth. His message asks his hearers to trust the Lord through the years of waiting.
Zacharias hears that Elisabeth will bear a son. John’s life will help prepare a people to receive the Lord.
The announcement comes to Mary with an invitation to trust God. Her question and willing response are part of the account Luke asks us to hear.
Their greeting becomes a moment of recognition and blessing. Elisabeth welcomes Mary as the mother of her Lord.
Joseph receives direction to take Mary as his wife and name the child Jesus. He rises ready to act on the message.
Joseph goes to Bethlehem with Mary. Their journey leads into Luke’s account of the Savior’s humble birth.
Mary wraps her firstborn Son and lays Him in a manger. The promised Savior has entered mortal life.
The shepherds hear news of great joy: the Savior is born. They are given a sign that will help them find the child.
The shepherds come with haste and share what they have heard. Mary keeps these things and ponders them in her heart.
Simeon gives thanks for the salvation he has lived to see. His witness welcomes the light prepared for all people.
Anna gives thanks to the Lord and speaks of the child to those looking for redemption. Her patient worship opens into a living witness.
The visitors find the child with Mary, worship Him, and offer their gifts. Matthew brings us into a house for this encounter.
Following the warning, Joseph takes the child and Mary toward Egypt. His prompt care protects the young family through danger.
Nephi pours out his sorrow for the believers. The Lord’s voice assures him that the promised sign will come.
The sun has gone down, yet the darkness does not come. The light and the new star fulfill the promised signs of the Savior’s birth.
The child’s name confirms the angel’s message. Zacharias’s voice returns in praise, and the neighbors share the family’s wonder.
Mary’s words celebrate God’s mercy and faithfulness. Her song joins personal gratitude to the hope of His people.
The family settles in Nazareth after their return. The Savior’s early years unfold within the daily care of a home.
